subject: SIG-Lite spot check: runtime keystore custody + escrow mapping
messages:
From: Daniel Park <dpark@novacorp.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@novacorp.com>, NovaCorp Security <security@novacorp.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 09:17:00 -0800
Subject: SIG-Lite spot check: runtime keystore custody + escrow mapping

Hi Ava —

Thanks again for the demo last week. As part of our standard SIG-Lite review for new vendors, our security team needs a focused spot-check on two areas before we proceed to procurement:

1) Runtime keystore custody: which subprocessor(s) hold keys used by your inference runtime (including KV cache and ephemeral session keys), and what access controls separate those keys from operator/admin accounts?

2) Ephemeral key escrow: do you provide (or require) an escrow path for ephemeral keys used during inference (for example, for PSPs or customer-managed KMS integration)? If yes, please share the operational runbook and residency constraints.

We don't need full SIG/CAIQ right now — just the targeted evidence to validate your claims in the vendor profile. If you have a short CSV roster and a brief runbook PDF, that would be ideal. Can you please share by COB Tuesday (2026-11-16)?

Appreciate it — happy to jump on a 20m call if helpful.

Thanks,
Daniel
Sr. Security Analyst
NovaCorp Health

From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood-inference.com>
To: Daniel Park <dpark@novacorp.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood-inference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood-inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SIG-Lite spot check: runtime keystore custody + escrow mapping

Thanks Daniel — we'll get this over. Looping in Ben (security/compliance) and Laura (infra) to assemble the short roster + runbook. Quick note up front:

- Runtime keys: our runtime uses a hybrid approach. Customer-managed KMS (optional) is supported via our private deployment flow; for hosted customers we separate long-lived signing keys (HSM-backed) and short-lived inference session keys (ephemeral) which are stored in an internal keystore service with strict RBAC and audited access.

- Escrow: we do not escrow customer-managed KMS keys. For Redwood-managed ephemeral keys we maintain an internal escrow snapshot facility used only for incident recovery; access is limited to a rotating on-call with multi-party approval. Residency is US-only by default, EU-by-request.

Ben and Laura, can you attach: (1) a one-page CSV roster listing subprocessors that have any keystore access, (2) the current ephemeral key escrow runbook PDF, and (3) a short note about RBAC separation controls? We should keep the bundle small — Daniel asked for a short CSV + runbook.

Ava
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood-inference.com>
To: Daniel Park <dpark@novacorp.com>
Cc: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood-inference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood-inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 08:47:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SIG-Lite spot check: runtime keystore custody + escrow mapping

Hi Daniel — attaching the two files you requested. Short summary below and a couple of clarifying notes.

Attachments:
- redwood_runtime_keystore_roster_20261114.csv (CSV: provider,role,access_scope,residency,contacts)
- ephemeral_key_escrow_runbook_v1.2.pdf (operational runbook, approvals flow, audit logging examples)

Summary: 
- Subprocessors with keystore access: three external providers appear on the roster: KeyHarbor (HSM provider, restricted signing key access), CacheWorks (KV cache provider, no key export), and LogStream (stores audit logs only; no key custody). We also list internal services (keystore-service, session-manager) as non-external entries.
- RBAC & separation: signing key ops are limited to our cryptography team and require MFA+tidy KMS IAM roles; ephemeral session key generation is handled by session-manager with ephemeral tokens that are not accessible via admin consoles.
- Escrow: the escrow snapshot is retained for 30 days and is encrypted with a separate escrow KMS key; access requires approvals from two senior engineers + on-call rotation entry. Residency: default US; EU residency available on Dedicated/Private plans with documentation.

Clarifying Qs (so we give exactly what you need):
1) Do you need evidence of key handling controls (e.g., KMS IAM policies) or is the CSV + runbook sufficient?
2) For procurement, do you require a CAIQ artifact now, or should we limit to SIG-Lite items to speed delivery?

If you prefer, we can redact specific internal principal emails from the CSV prior to sending to a larger audience.

-Ben
Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_runtime_keystore_roster_20261114.csv; ephemeral_key_escrow_runbook_v1.2.pdf

Subject: Re: SIG-Lite spot check: runtime keystore custody + escrow mapping

Ben / Ava — thanks, this is helpful and the bundle is what we expected. Procurement: this clears the technical evidence gating for vendor review pending a short legal review. Security team: two quick asks before we close the loop: (a) can you provide a redacted example of the escrow snapshot manifest (no secret material, just structure and retention tags), and (b) if EU residency is enabled for a Dedicated deployment, can you confirm the escrow key residency control will be scoped to the EU KMS without transitive US export?

Ben, if you can share the redacted manifest and a one-line confirmation about residency scope by EOD Wednesday we can cut the PO and loop legal. Happy to set a 15m call if easier.

Regards,
Daniel
Sr. Security Analyst
NovaCorp Health
